_instructions.how_to_use: This is the example the template ships with, so a fresh copy builds a real PDF straight away. Nothing in it names a real person or a real employer. Replace every value with your own.
_instructions.bullets: Write each bullet as: accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z. Lead with the outcome, not the task. Put a number in most of them. The bullets below show the shape to copy.
_instructions.length: One page for under ten years of experience. Cut the oldest role before you shrink the type. The build fails if either document runs to two pages.
_instructions.sections: section_order decides which sections appear and in what order. Remove a name from it and that section is gone from the PDF.
_instructions.ordering: Experience first once you have industry experience. Projects first while you are a student or changing field.
_instructions.separators: Write a plain | between items. The pre-processor typesets it.
_instructions.cover_letter_date: Leave cover_letter.date empty and the letter carries the build date.
_instructions.summary: Optional. Strong experience speaks for itself, so summary is left out of section_order here.

resume.summary: One line: your specialism, your strongest evidence, and the role you want.

bullets: Rebuilt the settlement pipeline serving 40M transactions a day, cutting end-to-end latency from 900ms to 120ms by replacing per-row lookups with a batched read path.
Designed the idempotency layer shared by 12 services, which removed duplicate charges entirely and reduced support escalations by 71%.
Traced an intermittent data loss affecting 0.3% of refunds to a silent retry in the message consumer, and fixed it by committing offsets only after a durable write.
Mentored three engineers through their first on-call rotation, after which mean time to acknowledge fell from 22 minutes to 6.
Built the ingestion service that backfilled four years of event history, 2.1B rows, without downtime on the live cluster.
Automated the weekly reconciliation report, removing nine engineer-hours a week of manual spreadsheet work.

projects.name: Project Name
bullets: What it does, and the part that was genuinely hard, measured by a benchmark rather than described as difficult.
A design decision you would defend in an interview, and the reason you chose it over the obvious alternative.

projects.name: Second Project
bullets: What it does and the result it produced, with the number that makes the result checkable.

skills.items: Cloud, Orchestration, Infrastructure as code, CI

education.detail: Thesis, award or relevant coursework. Delete this line if there is none.

publications.citation: Authors. Title of the paper. Venue, Year.

cover_letter.subject: Application for Job Title, REQ-0000
paragraphs: I am applying for the Job Title role. I work on your specialism, most recently the thing you shipped which produced the result, and I would like to do that work on the team or the problem named in the posting.

The work closest to yours is Project Name. State the hard part in one sentence, because that is what tells a reader you understood the problem rather than followed a tutorial. Say what you did and give the measured result. Then say why it resembles theirs.
Give a second piece of evidence of a different strength, and the outcome it produced. Operational judgement, mentoring or writing all count here, and none of them appear in a list of technologies.
I would welcome the chance to talk about a specific problem they have, named from the posting. Thank you for your time.
